description: Desde la década de 1960, la NASA ha dejado equipos y dispositivos tecnológicos en distintos lugares del sistema solar: en la Luna, en Marte y en el espacio profundo. Desde vehículos exploradores e instrumentos que completaron sus misiones científicas hasta sondas que aún continúan alejándose de la Tierra, estos equipos varían considerablemente tanto en su propósito como en su estado actual de funcionamiento.
summary:
“Spirit & Opportunity:  The Martian Water Test” is an interactive website that tells the story of Spirit and Opportunity, two twin robots designed by NASA as robotic geologists to explore the surface of Mars and search for evidence of water on the planet.
The main goal of the project is to encourage education, curiosity, and interest in space exploration among children, students, and space enthusiasts through a narrative, visual, and interactive experience.
Through this site, users will be able to learn about the story of both explorers, the challenges they faced, their scientific discoveries, and how they far exceeded the operating time they were designed for.
In this way, the project seeks to honor these robotic explorers that remain on Mars, highlighting their importance in the history of space exploration and the legacy they left for future missions.
details:
What exactly does it do?

Through an interactive narrative, this project aims to share the story of the twin rovers Spirit and Opportunity, describing the functions they performed, the objectives they set out to achieve, and the way their missions came to an end, in order to preserve the memory of their contributions to the exploration of the Red Planet.

It also seeks to foster interest in space, the equipment sent, the successfully completed missions, the goals achieved, and the conclusion of each one.

How does it work?

Purpose: To tell the story of two small robots who traveled millions of kilometers to a world that was not their own, and to share what they found there. We want to tell it dynamically and with empathy, so that people feel the journey, not just read about it.

Process: It began with curiosity. We learned about the mission, explored its history, and defined what we wanted people to feel. From there, we shaped the idea and made decisions for the presentation and the MVP (minimum viable product) as a local website. Finally, we brought it to life through design and implementation as a full website.

Stages (based on Design Thinking)

Template: Empathize → Define → Ideate → Prototype → Test

  1. Empathize: Research and read the stories of each of the NASA devices.
  2. Define: Define the design approach used to communicate the story and the audience it is meant for.
  3. Ideate: A website was planned to present the story.
  4. Prototype: The design was created and the website was programmed. The ideas and the multimedia elements created to convey the story were brought together.
  5. Test: The website was tested on a public site on the internet.

Main features: The story unfolds at the pace of the user: with every press of the down arrow key, a new chapter of the adventure appears. The 3D models are interactive, so users can get close to the rovers, turn them around, and discover each part of their design, as if they were standing beside them on the red soil of Mars. This gives the story an illustrative, almost tangible tone that invites users in and awakens their curiosity.

What benefits does it have?

Our project offers an educational, accessible, and entertaining way to learn about the history of space exploration through an interactive website.

One of its main benefits is making scientific and historical information easier to understand by turning it into a simple, engaging narrative for children, students, and space enthusiasts.

It also aims to spark curiosity, encourage independent learning, and motivate interest in science, technology, and space exploration.

Another important benefit is giving recognition to Spirit and Opportunity, highlighting their discoveries, the challenges they overcame, and their contribution to our knowledge of Mars.

Because it is a website, the project has the potential to reach a wider audience and be used as an educational support resource, promoting scientific knowledge in a more dynamic and approachable way.

This is seen as a good starting point for adding, in the future, the stories of other teams that were left behind on the Moon and Mars. Through these future stories, we hope to recognize their work and share the performance they achieved in their missions. 

What do you hope to achieve?

With this project, we hope to spark interest and curiosity in space exploration, especially among children, students, and enthusiasts, through an educational, visual, and interactive experience.

We want users not only to learn the story of these two inspiring robots, but also to understand the importance of their missions, the challenges they faced, and how their discoveries contributed to scientific knowledge of Mars.

We also want to show that technology and storytelling can be combined to turn complex scientific information into content that is accessible, engaging, and easy to understand.

In the long term, we hope this project can serve as an educational support tool that motivates new generations to take an interest in science, technology, and space exploration, keeping the legacy of Spirit and Opportunity alive and showing that even missions that have ended can continue to inspire new discoveries.
